Self-Awareness & Mind

Introduction to Professional Skills & Johari Window

Establishes the foundational distinction between technical, soft, and transferable competencies. Explores the internal compass shaping workplace character and introduces the 1955 Johari Window model for expanding interpersonal awareness.

Core Competencies:
→Distinguish between Technical Skills, Soft Skills, and Transferable Meta-Competencies.
→Analyze the four connected elements of Character Architecture: Values, Beliefs, Attitudes, and Outcomes.

Career Architecture

Portfolio Management & Engineering Your Digital Blueprint

Analyzes the four distinct archetypes of portfolios and articulates the end-to-end 3-phase engineering lifecycle. Emphasizes that 'Context is King' and details the rigorous assessment viva protocols.

Core Competencies:
→Categorize the 4 portfolio archetypes: Personal, Career/Dossier, Employment, and Assessment.
→Execute the 3-phase portfolio lifecycle: Strategy, Assembly, and Maintenance/Viva Defense.

03
Pillar 039 min read
Non-Verbal & Dialogue

Job Interviews & Mock Interview Skills

Demystifies the interview room as a two-way evidence-gathering dialogue. Breaks down Mehrabian's 93% non-verbal communication rule, the 6 C's (+ Confident) evaluation framework, and the STAR behavioral answering methodology.

Core Competencies:
→Master the three foundational questions underlying every interview question.
→Evaluate candidate performance using the 6 C's (+ Confident) framework.

Pillar 048 min read
Strategic Documentation

CV Writing & Career Documents

Details the structural anatomy of an ATS-compliant modern CV. Contrasts Chronological, Functional, and Combination formats, and establishes the definitive boundaries between a CV and a Resume.

Core Competencies:
→Identify the 6 essential anatomical sections of a winning curriculum vitae.
→Select appropriately between Chronological, Functional, and Hybrid CV formats.

Executive Communication

Speaking Skills & Effective Meetings

Explores the 7 C's of executive verbal delivery and examines meeting governance types. Provides the 10-point planning audit checklist to eliminate corporate meeting bloat and enforce timekeeping discipline.

Core Competencies:
→Apply the 7 C's of Executive Communication across verbal presentations and meetings.
→Distinguish between meeting typologies: Agile Standups, Customer Negotiations, Board Meetings, AGMs, and EGMs.

Digital Netiquette

Professional Email & Online Etiquette

Deconstructs the anatomical elements of high-impact professional emails. Establishes the 7 Golden Rules of Netiquette, addresses permanent digital archiving risks, and provides a dictionary of essential corporate abbreviations.

Core Competencies:
→Master the structural anatomy of an executive email: To/Cc/Bcc, Subject, Salutation, Body, CTA, Signature.
→Enforce the 7 Golden Rules of Netiquette to protect organizational and individual reputation.

Pillar 078 min read
Customer Service

Telephone Etiquette & Customer Service

Covers the mechanics of professional voice communications in client and technical support. Explores physiological vocal smiles, the 5 rules for placing callers on hold, and the HEAT/LAST method for defusing hostile interactions.

Core Competencies:
→Execute the 5 Steps to Telephone Excellence from prompt pickup to gracious closing.
→Understand the biomechanics of the vocal smile and how it alters vocal resonance.

Neuroscience & EQ

Emotional Intelligence & Brain Dynamics

Grounds emotional intelligence in evolutionary neuroscience. Analyzes Paul MacLean's Triune Brain Model, Daniel Goleman's Amygdala Hijack mechanism, Paul Ekman's 6 universal emotions, and the comparative value of EQ over IQ.

Core Competencies:
→Understand the three evolutionary layers of Paul MacLean's Triune Brain Model.
→Identify the neurobiological mechanism of the Amygdala Hijack and apply the 6-to-10 second respiration pause.

Executive Protocol

Dining Etiquette & Table Manners

Unpacks executive formal dining protocols for business dinners and diplomatic banquets. Details the 'Outside-In' silverware rule, the 'b' and 'd' spatial trick, Continental vs. American styles, silent utensil signals, and social taboos.

Core Competencies:
→Master the architectural geography of a formal multi-course table setting.
→Apply the 'Outside-In' cutlery progression rule and the 'b' and 'd' spatial mnemonic.
